entities.name: Abilio Martínez Varea
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abilio Martínez Varea (b. 1964) is a Spanish Catholic bishop serving as Bishop of Osma-Soria, one of the ancient Castilian sees whose history extends back to the Visigothic and early medieval periods. Born in Autol, La Rioja, he was ordained a priest of the Diocese of Calahorra and La Calzada-Logroño and was later appointed to episcopal office.

Osma-Soria is a diocese of great historical depth in the Castilian meseta — its cathedral city of El Burgo de Osma preserves a remarkable Romanesque-Gothic cathedral and was associated with the early formation of Saint Dominic Guzmán, founder of the Dominican Order, who studied there. The diocese's territory encompasses the province of Soria, one of the most sparsely populated regions of Spain and one facing severe demographic decline.

Martínez Varea's episcopal ministry engages the pastoral challenges of a diocese with deep Catholic roots but shrinking and aging population. Rural Castile's demographic crisis — young people leaving for Madrid and other cities, leaving elderly rural communities — presents one of the most difficult pastoral situations in contemporary Spanish Catholicism. His work represents the challenge of maintaining Catholic institutional life in a deeply traditional but rapidly depopulating region.
